sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 83

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XIII, List of Answers on Terminology 83:1
items.html: Of the ten surrounding Sefirot, there are only thirteen Sefirot in the beard: five Sefirot from Keter and nine Sefirot from Hochma, as in Answer 81 above. And their standing is such that the coarser something is, the lower is its place — that is, the opposite of the inner ones. For when the Sefirot shine in their stature, the coarser something is, the higher is its stature and the more upper it is; but this is only in the inner ones, namely when the lights are clothed in the vessels. But in the surrounding ones, meaning that the lights have distanced from the vessels, and coarseness does not cause the greatness of stature, therefore the coarser something is, the more inferior it is and the more lower. Hence the five Sefirot of Keter, which come from a stature higher than the nine Sefirot of Hochma, are found standing below the nine Sefirot of Hochma. And the Hesed of Keter is the lowest of them all, and the Malchut of Hochma is the highest of them all. (Page 392, Item 198; and in Or Pnimi there, s.v. 'behold').
